Turn 1 of 4 — read-back. Do not write any program JSON in this turn.

You are going to turn a workout into a Rhylthyme program: parallel **tracks** of sequential **steps**, each with a duration and a start trigger, that one person follows against a live clock.

Plan this as a Rhylthyme workout and deliver a live timeline: HIIT Circuit Card — three athletes, four stations for 3 athletes, 4 rounds
Resource limits: one rower, one kettlebell, one box, one sled, three athletes on the floor.
No finishing time was given; finish as early as the work allows.

Source text (read all of it):
<<<
HIIT Circuit Card — three athletes, four stations

Small group session, forty-five minutes on the clock including the warm-up and the stretch. There is one rower, one kettlebell, one box and one sled in the corner of the gym, and three of you. That means one station sits empty every round, and it means nobody ever waits on equipment if the rotation is respected.

The rule
Sixty seconds of work, all out, then sixty seconds of rest. Nobody starts a station until the athlete ahead of them has left it. If you are early, stand at the station and breathe; do not start.

Warm-up
Five minutes on the floor together: skipping, hip openers, shoulder pass-throughs, two sets of ten air squats. All three of you start at the same time and finish at the same time.

The stations
Rower: damper on five, pull hard, do not chase the split on the last ten seconds.
Kettlebell swings: one bell, hips not arms, chest tall at the top.
Box step-overs: alternate the lead leg, full extension at the top, no rebound.
Sled push: the length of the turf and back, low hands, short steps.

The rotation
Round 1: A on the rower, B on the kettlebell, C on the box.
Round 2: A on the kettlebell, B on the box, C on the sled.
Round 3: A on the box, B on the sled, C on the rower.
Round 4: A on the sled, B on the rower, C on the kettlebell.

Rest
Sixty seconds of rest on the floor after every station. Walk it off, do not sit down, do not lean on the next piece of equipment while somebody is still using it. There is no rest after the fourth station: that one runs straight into the cooldown.

Cooldown
Ten minutes on the floor when all three of you have finished the fourth station: easy bike or a walk, then quads, hips and thoracic spine. Nobody leaves early; the cooldown starts together.

Coach's note
The sled is the one that wrecks the rotation if somebody drags it. It is the longest reset and it is at the far end of the turf, so the athlete coming off the sled is the one most likely to hold up the person behind them. Watch that hand-off.
>>>

Read all of it before you answer. Then say back, in one paragraph and in your own words: what is being made, for how many (or at what scale), by when, and under what constraints — equipment that exists only once, how many people are working, anything that has to be held, rested or ready at a particular moment. If the text you were given looks truncated, or points at a section that is not here, say so instead of filling the gap.

End your reply with the same read-back as JSON in a single ```json fenced block:

```json
{
  "summary": "one paragraph: what is being made, for how many, by when, under what constraints",
  "servesOrScale": "8 people",
  "deadline": "2026-11-26T18:00:00",
  "constraints": ["one oven", "two burners", "two cooks"]
}
```

The workout is a small-group HIIT circuit for exactly three athletes (A, B, C) rotating through four stations — rower, kettlebell, box step-overs, sled push — over four rounds, with only three stations occupied at any moment since there are only three athletes for four stations. Each round is 60 seconds of all-out work followed by 60 seconds of rest, except the fourth round's stations run straight into the cooldown with no rest. The whole thing is bookended by a 5-minute warm-up that all three athletes start and finish together, and a 10-minute cooldown that begins only once all three athletes have finished their fourth station (nobody starts early). The binding constraints are single instances of each piece of equipment (one rower, one kettlebell, one box, one sled — each usable by only one athlete at a time), a fixed rotation schedule per round telling each athlete which station to use, and a strict no-overlap rule at hand-offs (an athlete may not start a station until the previous occupant has left it, even if that means standing and waiting). The text mentions "forty-five minutes on the clock" as a rough framing but gives no explicit deadline or start time, and per instructions I'm to schedule this to finish as early as the work and constraints allow rather than target that 45-minute figure or any wall-clock time. Nothing in the source appears cut off — the warm-up, four rounds of rotation, rest rule, cooldown, and coach's note about the sled are all fully present.

  "summary": "A three-athlete HIIT circuit rotating through four stations (rower, kettlebell, box step-overs, sled push) over four rounds of 60s work / 60s rest, with a synchronized 5-minute warm-up before and a 10-minute cooldown after that only starts once all three athletes finish their fourth station; equipment is single-instance (one of each station) and the fourth round has no rest before cooldown, so the schedule should finish as early as the constraints allow rather than hit any specific clock time.",
  "servesOrScale": "3 athletes, 4 stations, 4 rounds",
  "deadline": "none specified — schedule should finish as early as the work allows; the '45 minutes on the clock' mentioned is a rough framing, not a target or deadline",

    "one rower (single-use resource)",

    "three athletes total, each doing one station at a time",
    "fixed per-round rotation assigning each athlete to a station (one station idle per round)",
    "athlete may not start a station until the prior occupant has left it (strict hand-off, no early start)",
    "60s work then 60s rest after each of the first three rounds; no rest after the fourth round",
    "warm-up (5 min) must start and finish together for all three athletes",

completion.text:
**Restating the model:** A track is a single athlete's (or piece of equipment's) timeline of steps that run one after another with no overlap — since each athlete here does warm-up, then four stations with rests, then cooldown in strict sequence, each athlete is naturally one track. Each step declares exactly one duration kind — here everything is `fixed` (60s work, 60s rest, 5m warm-up, 10m cooldown) since none of it varies or runs indefinitely. Steps link to the clock or to each other via `startTrigger`: the warm-up steps use `programStart` (synchronized start), station and rest steps chain with `afterStep` off the previous step in that athlete's own track, and the cooldown for each athlete must wait on all three athletes' fourth stations, which likely needs a `compound` "all" trigger (or chaining off whichever athlete finishes last, resolved at validation/analysis time) so it truly starts together. `stepId`s must be unique across all three athlete tracks combined, not just within one, so I'll prefix them per athlete/round. Every station (rower, kettlebell, box, sled) is a `task` that must have a matching `resourceConstraint` with `maxConcurrent: 1` so the schedule enforces "nobody starts a station until the athlete ahead has left it," and the floor-based steps (warm-up, rest, cooldown) share a `floor` task with `maxConcurrent: 3` since all three athletes can be there together. Because each athlete's rotation is a fixed, distinct sequence of named stations (not n identical repeats of one unit of work), this is authored as explicit sequential steps per athlete rather than `replicates` — replicates would apply if, say, one athlete repeated the same station four times, which isn't the case here.

```json
{
  "acknowledgement": "tracks are sequential lines of work with no overlap; each step has exactly one duration kind (fixed/variable/indefinite); startTriggers (programStart, afterStep, compound, etc.) link steps to the clock or to each other; stepIds are unique across the whole program, not per track; every task a step occupies needs a matching resourceConstraint whose maxConcurrent enforces the one-at-a-time equipment rule; this workout's rotation is a fixed distinct sequence per athlete rather than n identical repeats, so it's authored as explicit steps, not replicates",
  "resourceConstraints": [
    { "task": "rower", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "kettlebell", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "box", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "sled", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "floor", "maxConcurrent": 3 }
  ],
  "actors": 3
}
```
